findings.title: StandardBounties.transferredAmountEqualsValue(uint256,uint256) uses a dangerous strict equality
findings.description:
A strict equality on a balance or amount can be broken by someone sending a little extra, locking the logic. Slither: StandardBounties.transferredAmountEqualsValue(uint256,uint256) (StandardBounties.sol#226-239) uses a dangerous strict equality:
	- require(bool)((tokenContracts[_bountyId].balanceOf(this) - oldBalance) == _amount) (StandardBounties.sol#233)

findings.title: Reentrancy in StandardBounties.issueAndActivateBounty(address,uint256,string,uint256,address,bool,address,uint256)
findings.description:
The function calls out to another contract before it finishes updating its own state. A malicious callee can re-enter while the state is half-written; no ether moves in the reentrant path itself, but the stale state can be abused. Slither: Reentrancy in StandardBounties.issueAndActivateBounty(address,uint256,string,uint256,address,bool,address,uint256) (StandardBounties.sol#320-357):
	External calls:
	- require(bool)(tokenContracts[bounties.length].transferFrom(msg.sender,this,_value)) (StandardBounties.sol#341)
	State variables written after the call(s):
	- bounties.push(Bounty(_issuer,_deadline,_data,_fulfillmentAmount,_arbiter,_paysTokens,BountyStages.Active,_value)) (StandardBounties.sol#345-352)
	StandardBounties.bounties (StandardBounties.sol#155) can be used in cross function reentrancies:
	- StandardBounties.acceptFulfil
